subject: Renewal proposal: tier shift, limited price-hold and sprint credit
messages:
From: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Patel <sophie@orem.ai>
Cc: Orem AI Procurement <procurement@orem.ai>
Date: Sat, 07 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal: tier shift, limited price-hold and sprint credit

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the chat last week. Per our conversation, attached is a concise proposal that aims to: (1) keep your unit economics stable through a short-term price-hold, (2) enable a tiered commit increase for August–December, and (3) provide a one-time sprint credit to accelerate your migration work. High level: 

- Term: 12 months (renewal effective 2027-09-01).
- Commit: increase to 1.5x current committed vCPU-hours (details in sheet). If you confirm the uplift, we can lock a 20% effective seat discount across the additional committed volume.
- Price hold: apply current unit price to all committed usage for 180 days from go-live (price resumes to standard thereafter unless we agree to an extension).
- Sprint credit: one-time $45,000 credit to be used for onboarding/engineering token spend (applies against billed usage).
- Burst credits: we can include 200k token burst credits for month 1 only (non-recurring).

Two quick notes: credits apply to invoices as a line-item offset (they reduce the invoice balance; they are not refundable). We require a PO or signed SOW to activate the sprint credit and price-hold.

Next steps: can you confirm whether procurement prefers (A) a single PO for the full 12-month commitment or (B) two POs (first 6 months, second 6 months) to match internal approval windows? If (A) works, we’ll generate a DocuSign-ready order form with the redlines pre-applied.

I’ve attached a short term-sheet (pdf) with the two commit tiers and the proposed invoice illustration. Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through.

—
Grace Oconnor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

From: Sophie Patel <sophie@orem.ai>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: Orem AI Procurement <procurement@orem.ai>
Date: Sat, 07 Aug 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: tier shift, limited price-hold and sprint credit

Hi Grace —

Thanks for the clear note and the term sheet. A few clarifying questions from procurement and finance before we escalate to legal: 

1) Price-hold vs discount: does the 20% discount apply only to the incremental committed volume, or to all committed volume (including the base)? Please show an invoice example if possible.
2) Credits: you said sprint credit applies against billed usage. Can those credits be applied to overage charges or are they limited to base/invoiceable committed usage?
3) PO cadence: procurement is leaning toward option (B) — two POs — because our Q3 approvals are split. Will the price-hold still be honored if we split the POs?
4) Billing: can we get month-by-month amortized price exposure in the order form so our finance team can model cashflow?

If you can respond with short answers and an updated one-page invoice illustration, we’ll fast-track to legal. We’re trying to close by next Wednesday (2027-08-11).

Appreciate it —
Sophie
Head of Platform Operations | Orem AI
sophie@orem.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 08 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal proposal: tier shift, limited price-hold and sprint credit

Grace / Marissa —

Replying with suggested guardrails from finance/legal so we can respond to SOPHIE’s questions inline: 

- Discounting: we should make the 20% discount explicit as applying to incremental committed volume only. That keeps baseline revenue intact and avoids complexity if they later step down. (Example included in redline doc.)
- Price-hold: agree to a capped 180-day price-hold on the committed baseline + incremental volume only if the first PO covers the first 180 days of committed billing. If they do two POs, we can still honor the hold provided the first PO documents the entire 180-day effective price-hold window (i.e., PO1 covers months 1–6 and references the price-hold through month 6).
- Credits: sprint credit must be applied to the invoice as an account credit and can be used for overages or committed usage unless otherwise specified. However, for audit and revenue recognition, credits that offset committed invoice lines will reduce recognized revenue and need to be amortized. We should call this out in the SOW.
- Burst credits: make burst credits month-1 only and non-recurring; cap token size and expire on day 30.
- Activation: require PO + signed order form referencing the attached SOW for activation.

I attached a redlined term sheet (redwood-term-sheet-redline.docx) with suggested language and a simple invoice illustration. Laura — please flag any legal issues re: amendment language (price-hold clause and credit accounting).

Thanks,
Ben
Head of Finance | Redwood Inference

From: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Patel <sophie@orem.ai>, Orem AI Procurement <procurement@orem.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: tier shift, limited price-hold and sprint credit

Hi Sophie — thanks for the quick review and great questions. Below are short answers and an updated plan to help procurement model this quickly. 

1) Discount scope: the 20% applies to the incremental committed volume only (i.e., the uplift above your current committed baseline). I’ve attached a one-line invoice illustration (see attached redline doc) that shows baseline vs incremental lines.

2) Credit application: the sprint credit is an invoice-level account credit. It can be applied to overage charges or committed invoice lines at your discretion. For clarity, we’ll add language to the SOW that credits reduce the invoice balance and are amortized where they reduce recurring committed invoice lines.

3) PO cadence & price-hold: two POs is fine. To keep the price-hold intact, PO1 should explicitly reference the 180-day price-hold window and note the second PO as "follow-on for months 7–12." We will honor the hold as long as PO1 documents the hold timeframe. If procurement wants, we can include a short clause in the order form to make that explicit.

4) Billing modeling: attached redline contains a month-by-month amortized exposure table (simple). If you prefer, Ben can send a CSV of amortized charges for your FP&A team to plug into your model.

Next steps: 
- If procurement confirms option (B) and will issue PO1 next week, I’ll have Ben and Marissa finalize the DocuSign order form by EOD Tuesday (2027-08-10).
- We’ll include the sprint credit as a line item and the 180-day price-hold clause in the order form.
- Please confirm preferred signatory for PO (billing/email) so we can match references in the order form.

Proposed quick call: Tuesday 08/10 at 11:00 PT to finalize PO wording and DocuSign link. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — excited to keep Orem moving forward.

Best,
Grace Oconnor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: redwood-term-sheet-redline.docx (redlines + invoice illustration), redwood-renewal-term-sheet-v1.pdf (proposal)
